FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Utensils, 
Cutlery and Domestic Hardware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering 
Divisional Council. 

This standard covers potable copper, stainless steel and aluminium bottle used for carrying of drinking water. 


This standard does not cover insulated and vacuum flask. Vacuum insulated flask is covered in IS 17526 : 2021 
‘Stainless steel vacuum flasks — Specification’. Insulated type of flask is covered in IS 17790 : 2022 ‘Insulated 
flask for domestic use — Specification’. 


While preparing this standard, assistance has been taken from BS EN 12546-1 : 2000 ‘Materials and articles in 
contact with foodstuffs. Insulated containers for domestic use: Part 1 Specification for vacuum ware, insulated 
flasks and jugs’. While implementing this standard, the manufacturer shall ensure compliance with relevant 
statutory regulations. 


The relevant SI units and corresponding conversion factors are given below for guidance: 


Pressure 1Pa(Pascal) = 1 N/m? 
1 kgf/mm? = 9.806 65 MPa 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


Indian Standard 


POTABLE WATER BOTTLES 
(COPPER, STAINLESS STEEL, ALUMINIUM ) — 


SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard covers minimum requirements of 
potable copper, stainless steel, aluminium bottle for 
carrying drinking water up to 1 500 ml. 


1.2 This Standard cover the addition requirements and 
shapes of aluminium bottle. Basic requirements of 
aluminium bottle are covered in IS 3603. 


1.3 This standard does not cover insulated and vacuum 
flask.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply. 


3.1 Domestic Copper Bottle — Potable bottle made 
of food grade copper, for carrying drinking water. 


3.2 Domestic Stainless Steel Bottle — Potable 
bottle made of food grade stainless steel for carrying 


drinking water. 


3.3 Domestic Aluminium Bottle — Potable bottle 
made of treated aluminium for carrying drinking 


water. 


NOTE — Refer 7.1.8 for treated aluminium anodic coating or 
hard anodised coating. 


3.4 Nominal Capacity — Volume of water at room 
temperature required to fill the bottle, when in upright 
position, to a level 10 mm below the lowest part of the 
inserted/screwed closure. 


IS 17803 : 2022 


4 TYPES (SHAPE, SIZE AND NOMINAL 
CAPACITY) 


4.1 The bottle normally comes in various capacities 
upto 1 500 ml. The nominal capacity of the bottle shall 
be declared by the manufacturer. 


4.2 The shape, size and nominal capacity of the bottle 
shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
manufacturer. 


5 MANUFACTURE AND WORKMANSHIP 


5.1 The bottle shall be clean, reasonably free from 
distortion, dents, wrinkles, wavy surface, colouring, 
burrs, scratches, pitting, deep tool marks and other 
surface defects. The design of the bottle shall be such 
that it is easy to clean and prevent accumulation of dirt. 


5.2 The bottle shall be subjected to tests as specified 
in 7. 


5.3 If possible, avoid welding and have only seamless 
stainless bottle. Welding if done for stainless steel 
bottle, shall be free from welding defects. The welding 
electrode shall conform to grade 308 or higher grade as 
per IS 5856. The weld shall be finished properly so that 
when a finger is passed on the joint, it shall be smooth. 


5.4 The mouth of the bottle which would be used for 
sipping shall have smooth, no sharp edges. 


5.5 Bottles shall be seamless drawn to avoid welding 
on copper or aluminium. 


6 SAMPLING 


For the purpose of conducting the tests, 3 samples of 
the bottle of each individual size shall be tested. In the 
event of one of the 3 samples failing the test, additional 
7 samples shall be tested and these shall all pass. 


7 PERFORMANCE TESTS 


7.1 Materials 
7.1.1 Copper Bottle 


7.1.1.1 The copper sheet used for drawing of bottle 
shall comply to the chemical properties as per cu- 
ETP, cu-FRHC or cu-CATH-2 given in Table 4 of 
IS 191. The minimum sheet thickness of bottle shall be 
0.5 mm. The minimum sheet thickness of lid and cap 
shall be 0.5 mm. The nominal thickness measured 
should the thickness at the place where little or no work 
has been done, at the base. 


7.1.2 Stainless Steel Bottle 


7.1.2.1 The material used to manufacture shall be 
of grade 304 as per IS 5522 or grade 316L as per 
IS 6911. The minimum sheet thickness of bottle shall be 


0.4 mm. The minimum sheet thickness of lid and cap 
shall be 0.4 mm. The nominal thickness measured 
should the thickness at the place where little or no work 
has been done, at the base. 


7.1.3 Stopper 


7.1.3.1 The stopper of the bottle shall be of non-toxic 
and food grade material (see IS 9845). If stainless steel, 
copper or aluminium is used, stopper shall conform to 
the material specified for the respective bottle. When 
fitted to the bottle it shall not slip off and shall provide 
a leak proof fitting. 


7.1.3.2 If an O-ring or washer is provided it shall be 
food grade silicone, refer to IS 3565 for information 
on silicone. Silicone manufacturers certificate for 
food grade is acceptable. Only physical and chemical 
properties needs to be complied with for silicone 
O-ring or washer. 


7.1.3.3 The O-ring or washer, when visually examined, 
shall be free from blisters, pinholes, cracks, embedded 
foreign matters and other defects which may impair 
their serviceability. No joints allowed 


7.1.4 Auxiliary Closure 


The auxiliary closure(s) can be made of polymer. It shall 
be non-toxic, food grade material and shall not deform 
under normal conditions of use (see to IS 9845 for 
compliance). The materials shall not contain bisphenol 
A (BPA). If auxiliary closure(s) is made of stainless 
steel, copper or treated aluminium, the material shall 
be same as that used for the bottle 


7.1.5 Lever, device for operating or regulating flow 
(if provided), should be made of food grade material. 
Supplier certificate for food grade is acceptable. The 
lever, device for operating or regulating of flow shall 
be operated for a minimum of 1 500 times. It shall be 
checked for proper functioning. 


7.1.6 Shoulder strap or cord to hang the bottle on a 
hook, if provided, shall comply with the respective 
requirements given in 7.4 or 7.5. 


7.1.7 Cord chain, if provided to hold the stopper/cap 
along with the bottle shall comply with the requirement 
as given in 7.6. 


7.1.8 The aluminium bottle, if treated with anodic 
coating shall comply to IS 1868. The minimum 
thickness of the anodic coating shall be 10 micron. The 
aluminium bottle, if hard anodised, shall comply to 
IS 6057. The minimum thickness of the hard anodized 
coating shall be 25 micron. 


7.1.9 The aluminium bottle if coated fully or partially 
externally, shall conform to the thickness test, salt 
water corrosion test, adhesion test procedures as per 
IS 9730. The limit for lead and cadmium of the coating 


shall be as per IS 9806 (see no iv and v of Table 1 
IS 9806), when measured as per standard test method. 
The minimum thickness of the coating shall be declared 
by the manufacturer. 


7.2 Capacity Test 


7.2.1 The nominal capacity of the bottle shall be 
declared amongst up to 1 500 ml. Bottles with other 
capacities may be manufactured as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the manufacturer. The tolerance on 
the nominal capacity shall be + 5 percent. No negative 
tolerance is permitted. The capacity of the bottle shall 
be checked as per 7.2.2. 


7.2.2 Ensure the bottle in empty. Take water in a 
calibrated jar. Pour the water from the calibrated jar 
into the bottle to a level 10 mm below the lowest part of 
the inserted closure. The difference in reading of water 
level in the calibrated jar is the capacity of the bottle.

7.3 Impact Resistance Test 
7.3.1 Drop Impact Test 


7.3.1.1 Fill water in the bottle up to its full capacity at 
the normal temperature and drop it horizontally from 
the height of 400 mm in a vertical state on a hard wood 
board of 30 mm or more in thickness fixed. 


7.3.1.2 The bottle shall be free from defects which are 
harmful to use. There shall be no crack or water leakage 
from the bottle. 


7.3.2 Pendulum Impact Test 


7.3.2.1 Fill water in the bottle up to its full capacity at 
the normal temperature. Raise the bottle to the position 
of 45° by making the length of the shoulder strap 
400 mm. Make the bottle collide with a hard wood 
board of 30 mm or more in thickness fixed vertically. 
Typical arrangement for test is shown in Fig. 1. 


Fic. 1 PENDULUM IMPACT TEST 


IS 17803 : 2022 


7.3.2.2 The bottle shall be free from defects which 
are harmful to use. There shall be no crack or water 
leakage. The bottle shall comply to leakage test as 
specified in 7.7. 


7.4 Test for Strength of Shoulder Strap 


7.4.1 A shoulder strap if provided, shall be subjected to 
the test as given in 7.4.1.1. 


7.4.1.1 Weigh the bottle with water filled to its maximum 
capacity along with the stopper(s) and auxiliary(s) as 
applicable. Apply a load, equal to a minimum of ten 
times its weight, typical arrangement as shown in Fig 2. 
After the maximum load is attained, keep for 5 min and 
examine the presence of any abnormality. 


FIG. 2 TEST FOR THE SHOULDER STRAP 


7.4.2 After or during this test, the strap shall not break. 
The area on the bottle to which the strap is fastened 
shall not show any signs of damage or defect. The 
elongation under load shall not exceed 10 percent of 
the total length of the strap. Initial stretching due to 
unwinding of the strap shall not be taken as elongation 
for the purpose of calculation. 


NOTE — The material of the strap may be flexible and shall 
not be affected by water. 


7.5 Test for Cord 


7.5.1 In case instead of a shoulder strap if a cord is 
provided to tag the bottle to a hook, the strength of the 
cord shall be subjected to the test as given in 7.5.1.2. 


7.5.1.2 Take a random sample other than that specified 
in 6. Put small steel balls equivalent to 2.5 times the 
weight of water that the bottle can hold. Hang the filled 
bottle by a suitable means. Ensure the bottle is hanging 
freely without touching any surface. Check the strap 
after 24 h, there shall be no visual defects or physical 
damage. The area on the bottle to which the strap is 
fastened shall not show any sign of damage or defect. 


7.6 Test for Cord Chain 


Take a random sample other than that specified in 6. 
Put small steel balls equivalent to 1.5 times the weight 
of water that bottle can hold. Hang the filled bottle by 
a suitable means. Ensure the bottle is hanging freely 
without touching any surface. Check the cord chain 
after 5 min, there shall be no visual defects or physical 
damage. The area on the bottle/cap to which the cord 
chain is fastened, shall not show any signs of damage 
or defect. 


7.7 Leakage Test 


7.7.1 Fill the bottle to 75 percent of its nominal capacity 
with water at 95 °C containing 0.5 percent surfactant. 
Close the stopper with a torque of 2 N.m or if not fitted 
with a screwed stopper, push in the stopper to its full 
extent. Thoroughly dry the outside of the stopper, sipper 
etc. Put the bottle upside down position for at least 
10 min. No drops shall appear on the stopper, sipper or 
on the surface on which the bottle has been over turned. 
The bottle shall be tested without the auxiliary cover, 
if the design of the bottle is provided with an auxiliary 
cover along with the stopper. 


7.7.2 The bottle shall be subjected to internal air 
pressure of 50 kPa (around 0.5 kgf/cm’) for 15 s, 
shall not show any sigh of leakage when immersed in 
water. The test shall be carried out as prescribed in 3 of 
IS 2471. 


7.8 Staining Test (Stainless Steel Bottle Only) 


7.8.1 The inner and outer surface of the bottle shall be 
thoroughly washed with hot soapy water. Thoroughly 
rinse and then degrease the test specimens in acetone 
or methylated spirits, then wiped using a soft cloth. The 
bottle, when dipped for 16 h in each of the following 
solutions maintained at 60 + 2 °C temperature, shall 
not show any sign of staining after removal from the 
solutions at the end of above period: 


a) Ten gram of glacial acetic acid (99 percent) 
dissolved in distilled water to make 100 ml; and 

b) Five gram of pure sodium chloride dissolved in 
distilled water to make 100 ml. 


7.9 Lever, Device for Operating or Regulating Flow 
Test 


Operate the lever or device 1 500 times and check 
for proper functioning of its intended use as per the 
instructions of manufacturer. 


7.10 Test for Stability of Bottle 


When the bottle filled with water to the full capacity 
is placed upright over a rough 10° inclined plane, it 
should not overturn or fall. 


7.11 Load Test 


Empty bottle in lid close condition apply the load 
test. Load of 5 kg shall be applied vertically on bottle 
surface for 30 min. There shall not be any deformation 
in shape/bulging. 


7.12 If any polymer material is used which comes in 
contact with the stored drinking water shall be food 
grade, shall comply to food safe test/leaching test as per 
IS 9845. The polymer used shall be BPA free. Supplier 
certificate is acceptable. The bottle shall not degrade 
the drinking water, the product shall comply with the 
test as per 5 of IS 8688. 


7.13 The bottle shall be properly rinsed with RO or 
distilled water. The bottle then shall be filled to capacity 
with RO or distilled water. Let it store for 24 h. The 
water when tested after storing for minimum 24 h, shall 
comply with the physical requirements of IS 10500. 


8 INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE 


8.1 Bottle shall carry adequate instructions to the user 
for its proper use to ensure satisfactory performance. 


8.2 The manufacturer shall provide the following 
minimum information along with each bottle as given 
below: 


a) How to unpack and take care of environment; 


IS 17803 : 2022 


b) How to stock the bottle in case the bottle is not 
going to be used, to avoid pitting or getting 
contaminated; 

c) Wash thoroughly before and after use; 

d) Always rinse with clean water before each use; 


e) Ensure the bottle is cleaned, empty and dry before 
stocking after each use; 


f) Do not use for carrying ice cubes; do not put in 
freezer. 


g) Do not use to store or carry carbonated drinks; 
h) The bottle should be periodically cleaned; 


j) Never use in a dishwasher, unless otherwise stated 
by the manufacturer; and 


k) Keep these instructions safe. 
9 MARKING 


9.1 Each bottle shall be legibly and permanently marked 
with the following minimum information: 
a) Nominal capacity; 
b) Grade of material of bottle along with applicable 
IS No.; 
c) Name or trade mark of the manufacturer; and 
d) Batch number. 


9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10 PACKAGING 


Each bottle shall be suitable packaged to avoid 
any damage during transit. The packaging shall be 
eco-friendly. 


IS 17803 : 2022

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
